questions.solution:
Both statements are true.

Ctrl + L and Ctrl + E are standard alignment shortcuts in Word, with Ctrl + L aligning text to the left and Ctrl + E centering it. These are part of the basic text formatting shortcuts.

The formatting shortcuts Ctrl + I (italic) and Ctrl + U (underline) can indeed be used in combination - you can press one after the other to apply both formats to the selected text. This is because Word allows multiple formatting attributes to be applied simultaneously to the same text.

questions.solution:
Ctrl + Shift + Esc: This shortcut opens the Task Manager.

Windows Key + L is the standard keyboard shortcut for locking your Windows computer. This immediately secures your session, requiring your password to log back in.

Ctrl + Alt + Del: This combination brings up a menu with several options, including "Lock," but it requires an extra step.

Windows Key + D: This shortcut minimizes all open windows, showing the desktop.

The Windows Key is the most common and direct way to open the Start Menu.

Ctrl + Esc: This will also open the Start Menu.

Alt + Esc: This shortcut switches between open applications, similar to Alt + Tab but without the visual preview.

Shift + Esc: This shortcut opens the Task Manager.

Ctrl + R: In some applications, this might be used for Redo.

Alt + R: This combination doesn't have a standard function in most Windows contexts.

Shift + R: This does not have a standard assigned function in Windows itself.

questions.solution:
Ctrl + Spacebar selects the entire column in the active cell.

Shift + Spacebar: This shortcut selects the entire row.

Ctrl + Shift + Spacebar: This shortcut selects the entire worksheet if a cell is selected, or the current region if a range is selected.

Alt + Spacebar: This shortcut opens the Control menu for the Excel window.

Ctrl + D (for "Down") copies the contents (including formulas) from the cell above the selected cell(s) and pastes them into the selected cell(s). This is very useful for quickly applying a formula to a range of cells in a column.

Alt + Enter is indeed used to create a new line within the same cell in Excel - this is essential for formatting text within cells without creating a new row. This statement is true.

The second statement is false. Both F4 and Ctrl + Y actually repeat the last action in Excel. Ctrl + Z (not Ctrl + Y) is the shortcut that undoes the last action.

Ctrl + ; is the shortcut for inserting the current date in Excel.

Ctrl + : This shortcut inserts the current time in Excel.

Alt + D or Alt + ;: These shortcuts don't have a built-in function for inserting the date in Excel.

questions.solution:
Both statements are correct. F5 is the standard shortcut to start a presentation from the first slide, while Shift + F5 starts from the current slide - these are essential shortcuts for presenting efficiently.

The sequence Alt + H + F + F is indeed the correct keyboard sequence to access the fonts dropdown menu. This is part of PowerPoint's KeyTips system, where Alt reveals keyboard shortcuts for ribbon commands, and subsequent key presses navigate through the menu options (H for Home tab, F for Font group, F for Font dropdown).
